 The board of directors (the “ Board ”)
of Alibaba Group Holding Limited (“ Alibaba Group ” or the “ company ”) is pleased to announce that
the unaudited consolidated results of the company, its subsidiaries and consolidated entities (the “ Group ”) for the
three months and the six months ended S eptember 30, 2026. The Group’s unaudited consolidated financial statements have
been prepared under accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (“ U.S. GAAP ”) and reviewed by the
audit committee (the “ Audit Committee ”) of the Board.
 In this results announcement, “we,” “us,” and
“our” refer to the company and where the context otherwise requires, the Group.
 1 
 “Our full-stack AI capabilities continue to improve commercialization
and delivered a strong quarter. Growth in Alibaba Cloud’s recurring revenue from external customers was 67%, which drove an acceleration
of overall cloud revenue growth with significantly improving profitability. AI-related product revenue delivered triple-digit growth for
the thirteenth consecutive quarter. We recently announced comprehensive upgrades spanning proprietary chips, supernode architecture, agent-native
cloud infrastructure, AI models and agents. Notably, T-Head unveiled its next-generation Zhenwu V900 AI chip. In our consumption business,
Alibaba E-commerce Group’s profitability improved significantly. Quick commerce continued to narrow its losses substantially while
maintaining market share,” said Eddie Wu, Chief Executive Officer of Alibaba Group. “We will continue to bring technological
innovations to our comprehensive AI stack to meet the strong and diverse AI demands across industries.”
 “This quarter, our business delivered strong growth in both revenue
and earnings because of our strategic focus on AI + Cloud growth and profit sustainability in Alibaba E-commerce Group. Cloud segment
revenue growth continued to accelerate, with quality earnings further driving EBITA margin up to 14.5%. The e-commerce segment delivered
significant EBITA growth, driven by improving unit economics in quick commerce and solid growth of marketplace e-commerce,” said
Toby Xu, Chief Financial Officer of Alibaba Group. “As AI monetization continues to ramp up, we will maintain disciplined investments
in AI capabilities with a focus on return on invested capital while targeting to achieve positive free cash flow.”

 BUSINESS AND STRATEGIC UPDATES 
 Alibaba E-commerce Group 
 During the quarter, we sustained revenue
stability with CMR decreasing 5% year-over-year and growing 1% on a like-for-like basis if the contra revenue impact from the new business
development program were excluded. Adjusted EBITA of the group achieved 243% year-over-year growth this quarter, primarily driven
by a significant loss reduction in the China Quick Commerce business. In addition, our China E-commerce business contributed to stable
operating profit and the Global Wholesale business delivered strong profits, while we reduced losses in the International E-commerce business.
 We have continued to advance our strategic
priorities of unlocking significant synergies across our domestic and cross-border businesses, and deepening the integration of AI capabilities
across our e-commerce platforms. Recent progress includes the integration of management across our domestic and international wholesale
businesses, as well as the launch of QwenWork E-commerce for merchants, an AI product powered by our agentic AI capabilities, in
October.
 QwenWork E-commerce is integrated
into QwenWork, our one-stop AI agent platform, and is designed to automate end-to-end merchant workflows, including store operations,
business analytics, advertising and customer service. Leveraging our existing merchant tools, it connects directly to Taobao and Tmall
data and will further support data access across other platforms, enabling more seamless cross-platform operations. In addition, by leveraging
Qwen model family’s advanced multimodal capabilities, we are able to better understand complex consumer needs and deliver more relevant
product recommendations with knowledge-based reasoning. These enhanced capabilities have driven a notable increase in general knowledge-related
queries, creating more opportunities to identify latent consumer demand, facilitate product discovery, and drive sales conversion.
 In our China Quick Commerce business, Taobao Instant Commerce continued
to improve its unit economics quarter-over-quarter while maintaining market share. This reflected higher average order value, as we further
improved the order mix through an increasing focus on high-value food and non-food categories. Meanwhile, Freshippo maintained its robust
growth across online and offline channels, driven by deeper collaboration with Taobao Instant Commerce and the expansion of its multi-format
store network that offers differentiated products to diverse demographics.
 The number of 88VIP members, our highest
spending consumer group, continued to increase by double digits year-over-year to approximately 66 million as of September 30, 2026.
The ARPU of new 88VIP members, defined as those who joined the membership program within the past year, increased significantly year -over-year
during the 11.11 Global Shopping Festival. We remain focused on the growth and retention of 88VIP members through enhanced value proposition
to our most valued customers.
 Xianyu is China’s leading consumer-to-consumer
community and marketplace for idle goods. It makes buying and selling more convenient for consumers and small businesses through AI-powered
features including smart pricing, automated product listing descriptions and precise buyer targeting, as well as consignment services.
This quarter, Xianyu continued its strong growth momentum, with daily active users and paid orders up 23% and 29% year -over-year,
respectively.
 4 
 AI Cloud and Compute Services 
 For the quarter ended September 30,
2026, revenue from AI Cloud and Compute Services was RMB60,973 million (US$9,094 million), a 53% increase from the same quarter last year.
The growth of revenue from external customers accelerated to 64% year-over-year. The growth of recurring revenue from external customers,
which excludes compute equipment solutions revenue, also accelerated to 67% year-over-year. In particular, AI-related product revenue
continued to show strong momentum, achieving RMB17,918 million (US$2,673 million) and delivering the thirteenth consecutive quarter of
triple-digit year-over-year growth. The strong growth reflected broad-based demand for our AI + Cloud services. Beyond training
and inference workloads at AI labs, customers across the internet, automotive, embodied AI, financial services and biotechnology sectors
rapidly expanded their use of our cloud services to support innovation and grow their business.
 Cloud 
 Alibaba Cloud continued to strengthen our market-leading full-stack
AI capabilities, as demonstrated by the comprehensive upgrades unveiled at the Apsara Conference in September, spanning proprietary chips,
supernode architecture, agent-native cloud infrastructure, AI models and agents. These advancements across our co-designed and integrated
stack have accelerated enterprise adoption and deeper integration into core business workflows, enabling us to capitalize on increasingly
diverse demand across industries.
 Our ability to empower enterprise AI adoption has earned notable recognition
in the 2026 Gartner® Magic Quadrant™ for Strategic Cloud Platform Services, a report that comprehensively evaluates how cloud
service providers support the entire enterprise cloud lifecycle. Alibaba Cloud was named a Leader in the highest quadrant, making it the
first and only Asia-Pacific provider to receive this distinction.
 Chip Design – T-Head Semiconductor (“T-Head”) 
 By rapidly advancing its portfolio of proprietary chips and software,
T-Head further strengthened the infrastructure foundation underpinning our AI capabilities.
 At the Apsara Conference in September, we unveiled the Zhenwu V900,
our next-generation AI chip for training and inference, with commercial release scheduled for the first quarter of 2027. Built on our
proprietary parallel computing architecture, the Zhenwu V900 delivers significant performance improvements over its predecessor, the Zhenwu
M890. We also open-sourced T-Head SAIL, the software stack for Zhenwu chips, to simplify application migration, expand developer adoption,
and strengthen compatibility with mainstream AI frameworks.
 In addition, we launched the Zhenwu M890 supernode instance in August,
marking the introduction of China’s first supernode architecture capable of supporting inference for models with more than
two trillion parameters. At the Apsara Conference, we also showcased our next-generation supernode product, which integrates the Zhenwu
V900 with other proprietary interconnect, networking, and storage chips, and is scheduled for launch in the first quarter of 2027.
 5 
 AI Labs and Applications 
 Model 
 We continued to advance our comprehensive model portfolio, with a primary
focus on foundation models, while enhancing capabilities across video, audio, image and music. This demonstrates our industry leadership
and rapid pace of iteration.
 Recently, we launched Qwen4-Max, built on the new mixture-of-experts
architecture with 2.4 trillion backbone parameters and native visual capabilities. Qwen4-Max advances productivity and token efficiency,
delivering stronger long-horizon task execution across industries, including manufacturing, game development, healthcare, and frontier
scientific research.
 QwenWork 
 Our agentic platform QwenWork continued to gain traction across industries,
driven by ongoing enhancements to its enterprise capabilities. At the Apsara Conference in September, we launched Enterprise Context,
a solution that continuously organizes and updates enterprise information and knowledge across company documents, meeting records and
internal communications. It enables AI agents to access company-specific information and execute tasks based on organizational knowledge
and workflows.
 Qwen App 
 Qwen app for individual users now provides personalized assistance
for tasks across more than 20 service categories, including shopping, local services, travel, work, learning, personal finance and health,
leveraging Alibaba’s ecosystem and third-party partnerships. In October, we launched Qwen Go!, a cloud-based personal agent embedded
within the Qwen app. Qwen Go! autonomously executes multi-step tasks across platforms, while retaining contextual information and user
preferences over time to deliver increasingly personalized assistance across everyday activities.
 All Others 
 Our store guide and mapping platform Amap offers consumers one-stop
access to services such as navigation, to-destination services and ride-hailing. On October 1, 2026, the first day of National Day
holiday in China, Amap recorded an all-time high of approximately 370 million peak daily active users. Leveraging Amap Street Stars, a
feature that provides a trust-based rating system to support users’ consumption decisions, Amap has strengthened its mindshare in
local services across consumption use cases, including dining, tourist attractions and seasonal activities.
 Share Repurchases 
 During the quarter ended September 30, 2026, we repurchased a
total of 17.95 million ordinary shares (equivalent to approximately 2.24 million ADSs) for a total of US$221 million. These purchases
were made in the U.S. market under our share repurchase program.
 Capital Expenditures 
 During the quarter ended September 30, 2026, capital expenditures
were RMB50,477 million (US$7,529 million), an increase of 60% compared to RMB31,501 million in the same quarter of 2025, due to continued
investments in AI infrastructure to meet strong and accelerating customer demand. The significant year-over-year increase was due to an
acceleration in scaling compute capacity, higher pricing of a broad range of chip components, an increase in CPU-compute capacity driven
by anticipated growing customer adoption of AI agents, and fluctuations in procurement cycles.
 In addition to training and inference demand from AI Labs, we continue
to see robust demand from customers in China’s emerging innovation economy, including electric vehicles (EVs), embodied AI, and
biotechnology. Scale is becoming an increasingly critical competitive advantage in cloud computing, providing us with orchestration flexibility,
operating efficiency and cost advantages. By investing in infrastructure today, we aim to extend our scale leadership, strengthen our
supply chain and reinforce our long-term competitive position.
